intro.html: If customers can't find your website on Google, it may as well not exist. My SEO audit gives you a clear picture of why your site is, or isn't, getting found, and a fix plan in order of impact. Then I can make the fixes for you, safely, on a staging copy first.

blocks.html: Most small business sites don't need more content to rank. They need the basics fixed. These are the issues I see most often:

items.h: The site is hidden from Google.
items.html: A single WordPress setting, "Discourage search engines", is left on after launch and blocks the whole site.
Google has crawled them but chosen not to show them, often because of thin or duplicate content.
Every page shares the same title, or has none, so Google can't tell them apart.
A redesign changed URLs without redirects, and the pages that used to rank now return errors.
Oversized images and too many plugins drag down Core Web Vitals, especially on phones.
Opening hours, service areas or addresses differ between the site, Google Business Profile and directories.
Google has to guess what the business is, where it works and what it offers.

blocks.html: I check robots settings, your XML sitemap, canonical tags, noindex tags and Google Search Console's coverage report, so we know which pages Google can reach and which it actually shows.
I find pages that compete with each other, copied text across pages, and pages too thin to rank. For each one I recommend whether to merge, rewrite or remove it.
Titles, meta descriptions, headings, image alt text and internal links, checked page by page against the keyword each page should target.
Using Search Console data, I show which searches already bring impressions, which pages are close to page one, and where the quickest wins are.
Core Web Vitals, image sizes, plugin load and how the site behaves on a phone.
Name, address and phone consistency, service areas, opening hours and structured data for your business.

intro.html: The questions people ask most before starting a website project. If yours isn't here, ask me directly.

items.q: How much does a website cost?
items.a: Most small business websites cost between $900 and $3,500. The price depends on the number of pages, features such as booking or ecommerce, and whether you need copywriting. You get a fixed quote after a free audit, so you know the full cost before you commit.

items.q: How do payments work?
items.a: 50% to start and 50% at launch. Larger projects are split into milestones, so you only pay as work is approved. Payment is by bank transfer, Wise, PayPal or card.

items.q: Are there ongoing costs?
items.a: You'll pay for your domain and hosting directly, usually $80–$250 per year. Premium plugins such as Elementor Pro have yearly licences. Maintenance from me is optional.

items.q: Can I hire you through Fiverr?
items.a: Yes. You can order through my Fiverr profile or work with me directly. Prices are the same either way. Fiverr adds its own small service fee, and working directly gives you more flexible milestones.

items.q: How long does a website take?
items.a: A typical business site takes 3–5 weeks from the first call to launch. Simple sites can be faster; custom plugins and apps take longer. You get a dated plan with the quote.

items.q: What slows a project down?
items.a: Waiting for content is the most common delay. Having your text, photos and logins ready makes the biggest difference.

items.q: Should I use WordPress, Wix, Squarespace or Shopify?
items.a: WordPress suits sites that will grow, need custom features or want full SEO control. Shopify suits product stores. Wix and Squarespace suit simple sites you want to manage in one place. I work on all of them, so I'll recommend whichever fits.

items.q: Do I own my website?
items.a: Yes. Your domain, hosting, website and all accounts are in your name. Nothing is locked to me.

items.q: Can I edit the website myself?
items.a: Yes. WordPress sites are built with Elementor, so you can change text, images and pages visually. Every project includes video tutorials.

items.q: Do you provide hosting?
items.a: I don't host sites myself, but I'll recommend a host that fits your budget and set it up for you, so you own the account.

items.q: Will my website be on Google?
items.a: Every site launches with SEO foundations: unique page titles and descriptions, a sitemap, structured data and Search Console setup. Ranking for competitive searches takes time and depends on your market.

items.q: Do you guarantee rankings?
items.a: No one can honestly guarantee a Google position. I guarantee the technical setup is correct and that every issue I find is fixed properly.

items.q: Will I lose my rankings if I redesign?
items.a: Not if it's done carefully. I map your existing pages and set up redirects so the pages Google already trusts keep their value.

items.q: Where are you based?
items.a: In Bangladesh. I work with clients in the US and Europe and schedule calls around your time zone.

items.q: How do we communicate?
items.a: By email, WhatsApp, Fiverr or video call. You get updates at each milestone and I reply within 12 hours on working days.

items.q: What do you need from me to start?
items.a: Your website address (or idea), your goals, and access to your domain and hosting when we begin. I'll send a checklist after the call.

items.q: How many revisions are included?
items.a: Two rounds of revisions at the design stage and two at the build stage. Small text changes after launch are covered during the support period.

items.q: What support do I get after launch?
items.a: 30 days of free fixes for anything that isn't working as agreed.

items.q: Do you offer maintenance?
items.a: Yes: updates, backups, security checks and small edits from $79 per month.

items.q: Can you take over a site someone else built?
items.a: Yes. I'll audit it first and tell you what's worth keeping.

cases.h1: Safi Cleaners: a house cleaning website that books jobs
cases.title: Safi Cleaners: House Cleaning Website | Rakib Hasan
cases.summary: A local cleaning company's WordPress site that turns visitors across Hampden County into fixed-price quote requests.
cases.alt: Safi Cleaners website on a laptop
p_client: Safi Cleaners is a locally owned house cleaning business in Ludlow, Massachusetts. It serves Ludlow, Springfield, Chicopee, Wilbraham, Longmeadow, West Springfield and the rest of Hampden County. Services cover residential cleaning, Airbnb turnovers, deep cleans, move-in and move-out cleans, recurring plans, organising, and office cleaning.
p_challenge: People choosing a cleaner worry about price surprises and whether they can trust someone in their home. The site needed to answer both quickly and make booking feel low-risk.
p_built: A site with a clear page for each service, a list of the towns served, and a "How it works" section. A free quote form collects the service, property details, schedule and contact information, so the team can give a fixed quote before booking. Trust builders include reviews, a "Why us" section and the company's free 24-hour re-clean promise. Opening hours and contact details sit on every page.
p_result: Quote requests now arrive through the site every week, with the size of the home and the cleaning type already included.
p_testi: > "Rakib made our small business look as professional as the big names. Quotes come in every week now." — Emaina, Safi Cleaners
